notes: CSA is the leading cloud security standards body. Industry standard (CCM used in thousands of organizations), vendor neutral, expanding into AI security. Publishes control frameworks (CCM, AICM), runs the STAR certification program (public compliance attestations), and conducts AI security research through its AI Safety Initiative.

data.description: The de facto standard for cloud security controls, organized by domains containing controls.
data.notes:
Version 4.0 released 2021 (197 controls), updated to v4.1 (207 controls, 283 CAIQ questions). 17 domains. Domain code + two-digit control number (e.g., IAM-01). Maps to ISO 27001, NIST, PCI-DSS. Used for STAR certification.

No per-control web pages exist. Resolution returns a download URL and extraction instructions. The download is a ZIP bundle containing multiple files: the main spreadsheet, implementation guidelines, auditing guidelines, mappings, and CAIQ questionnaire.

Extraction instructions: (1) Download the ZIP from the download URL. (2) Unzip the bundle. (3) Open the main Excel file (e.g., 'CCMv4.1.1-generated_at_2026_10_02.xlsx'; cell A1 stamps the patch level). (4) Go to the 'CCM' sheet. (5) Columns: Control Domain (full name), Control Title, Control ID (format XXX-NN), Control Specification (full text). Additional columns contain applicability/ownership matrices, architectural relevance, and organizational relevance. (6) Find the row where Control ID matches.

Alternative: A machine-readable bundle (JSON/YAML/OSCAL) is available for programmatic access, but as of 2026-10-23 it is still the 4.1.0 release; 4.1.1's mappings and reworded text are only in the spreadsheet.

Domain codes are 2-3 uppercase letters, except A&A (Audit & Assurance) and, from 4.1, I&S (Infrastructure Security, formerly IVS), which contain an ampersand. The pattern must account for this. Each version node enumerates its own release's domain codes.

data.description: Security controls specific to AI/ML systems, complementing CCM for AI workloads.
data.version_disambiguation: AICM control IDs are NOT stable across releases. Between 1.0.3 and 1.1.0, CSA renumbered controls in place: 54 of the 242 control IDs present in both releases designate a DIFFERENT control. LOG-15 was Output Monitoring in 1.0.3 and is Input Monitoring in 1.1.0; IAM-12 was Safeguard Logs Integrity and is Unique Identities; TVM-12 was Threat Analysis and Modelling and is Vulnerability Management Metrics. Only one ID (IAM-19) disappeared outright, so comparing ID sets between releases does NOT detect this. 1.1.1 did NOT renumber: it carries the same 247 control IDs, titles, and 18 domains as 1.1.0, so a 1.1.0 control ID names the same control in 1.1.1. Always cite AICM controls with an explicit version. Never migrate a reference between the 1.0 and 1.1 series by string match — CSA publishes no crosswalk, so the mapping has to be reconstructed by comparing specification text between the two releases.

versions_available.note: 247 controls across 18 domains, with the same control IDs, titles, and domain codes as 1.1.0 -- no renumbering. What changed from 1.1.0, per CSA's own dataset (csa-mcp): every control gains NIST AI RMF / NIST AI 600-1 and AIUC-1 (Q2 2026) cross-framework mappings with gap levels and addenda, restoring the NIST AI 600-1 coverage the 1.1.0 workbook dropped; the Model Provider implementation guidance for GRC-01, IAM-13, and IAM-18 was replaced (1.1.0 carried text written for other roles there); and the SEF-06 assessment question was reworded. The companion questionnaire stays AI-CAIQ 1.1.0 -- CSA did not issue an AI-CAIQ 1.1.1. Release date not asserted: CSA's v1.1 artifact page still reads "Released: 06/22/2026" (the 1.1.0 date) and does not name the patch level, and CSA publishes no changelog.

aliases.note: CSA's artifact page, bundle ZIP, and PDF titles brand the 1.1 line "v1.1" without a patch level. 1.1 resolves to the newest 1.1.x release, 1.1.1, because that is what CSA's own tooling does: the csa-mcp server resolves the series label aicm 1.1 to 1.1.1. A two-part label pointing at a patch release is a compromise -- it means 1.1 moves when CSA ships a newer 1.1.x. Cite @1.1.0 or @1.1.1 when the exact release matters.

versions_available.note: 247 controls across 18 domains. Control IDs renumbered in place from 1.0.3 — see version_disambiguation. Superseded by 1.1.1, which keeps every control ID. The workbook's Scope Applicability (Mappings) sheet dropped from 16 columns to 13: it carries BSI AI C4, the EU AI Act, and ISO/IEC 42001:2023, and no longer carries the NIST AI 600-1:2024 block that the 1.0.3 workbook included (1.1.1 restores NIST AI 600-1 mappings). CSA does publish a standalone NIST mapping artifact, but it is titled "AICM v1.0 mapping to NIST 600-1" and is keyed to pre-1.1.0 control IDs, which do not carry over. Addressable only as 1.1.0; the 1.1 and v1.1 labels resolve to 1.1.1.

243 controls. Its workbook carries the NIST AI 600-1:2024 mappings that the 1.1.0 workbook does not. Control IDs are not interchangeable with 1.1.0. CSA maintains a separate artifact record per major line: https://cloudsecurityalliance.org/artifacts/ai-controls-matrix is "AI Controls Matrix v1" (released 2025-07-09, updated 2025-10-30) and covers the 1.0.x line, while v1.1 has its own record. Version-specific companion artifacts also exist under CSA's aicmv1-0-3-* slug convention. Release date not asserted: upstream sources conflict (2025-11-10 in one index, a bare "2024" in the release metadata), and CSA publishes no changelog that settles it. CSA's v1 artifact record shows "Updated: 2025-10-30", a third candidate.

data.notes:
Current release is 1.1.1 (247 controls; same control IDs as 1.1.0, adds NIST AI 600-1 and AIUC-1 mappings). 1.1.0 (247 controls, 2026-06-22) is superseded by it. The labels 1.1 and v1.1 resolve to 1.1.1, matching CSA's csa-mcp server. 1.0.3 (243 controls) is superseded; its workbook carries the NIST AI 600-1:2024 mappings that the 1.1.0 workbook dropped. Releases 1.0.0 (July 2025) through 1.0.2 existed and were superseded by 1.0.3; none has a retrievable artifact or a CSA version-specific page, so they are not declared as resolvable versions here. Control IDs are NOT stable between 1.0.3 and 1.1.0 -- see version_disambiguation. Extends CCM for AI workloads. Shares all 17 CCM domains and adds MDS (Model Security) for 18 total. Control ID format is the same as CCM (XXX-NN), NOT the AI-prefixed codes previously assumed. Addresses model training security, data poisoning prevention, inference security, model theft protection, bias and fairness controls, and AI supply chain security. Aligns with NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, BSI AI C4.

Distinguishes between 'Cloud & AI Related' controls (shared with CCM) and 'Strictly AI Related' controls (AICM-only).

No per-control web pages exist. Resolution returns a download URL and extraction instructions. The download is a ZIP bundle containing: the main AICM spreadsheet, AI-CAIQ questionnaire, implementation guidelines, auditing guidelines, and framework mappings.

Extraction instructions: (1) Download the ZIP from the version node's download URL. (2) Unzip the bundle. (3) Open the main AICM spreadsheet. (4) Go to the controls sheet. (5) Columns: Control Domain (full name), Control Title, Control ID (format XXX-NN), Specifications (full text). Additional columns for five pillars: Control Type, Control Applicability/Ownership, Architectural Relevance, LLM Lifecycle Relevance, Threat Category. (6) Find the row where Control ID matches.

Use both CCM and AICM for comprehensive AI cloud security coverage.

data.description: Standardized self-assessment questionnaire mapping yes/no questions to CCM controls. One or more questions per CCM control.
data.notes:
CAIQ is the assessment-question form of CCM controls. Each CCM control has one or more yes/no questions used for cloud provider self-assessment and customer due diligence. CAIQ v4.0.3 contains 283 questions across the 207 CCM v4.1 controls.

Question IDs follow the format XXX-NN.M where XXX-NN is the parent CCM Control ID and M is the question sequence within that control (e.g., IAM-01.1, A&A-01.2). Multiple questions per control are common.

Distributed in the same ZIP bundle as CCM. The CAIQ is a separate sheet/tab within the bundle's main Excel file.

No per-question web pages exist. Resolution returns a download URL and extraction instructions.

Extraction instructions: (1) Download the CCM ZIP bundle. (2) Open the standalone questionnaire ('CAIQv4.1.0-star_security_questionnaire-generated_at_2026_10_02.xlsx', sheet 'CAIQv4.1.0'), or the 'CAIQ' sheet of the CCM workbook ('CCMv4.1.1-generated_at_2026_10_02.xlsx'). (3) Find the question there. (4) Columns: Question ID (XXX-NN.M format), Control ID (parent CCM control), Consensus Assessment Questions (the question text), Consensus Assessment Answers (where assessors record yes/no/NA). (5) Find the row where Question ID matches.

Used for STAR Level 1 self-assessments. Versions track CCM versions but with their own minor numbering.

data.description: Public registry of cloud provider security assessments. The largest public collection of CAIQ submissions. Listed here for discoverability — STAR is an index/registry of assessments, not itself a set of controls. The underlying assessment instrument is CAIQ (see ccm-caiq).
data.notes:
STAR is a registry/index of submitted security assessments, not a control framework. It is included in the control namespace for discoverability — the controls being assessed are CCM (see secid:control/cloudsecurityalliance.org/ccm), and the assessment questionnaire is CAIQ (see secid:control/cloudsecurityalliance.org/ccm-caiq).

Three assessment levels:
- Level 1: Self-assessment via CAIQ (free; publicly downloadable submissions). The largest portion of the registry.
- Level 2: Third-party audit (STAR Certification based on ISO 27001, STAR Attestation based on SOC 2).
- Level 3: Continuous monitoring (planned/emerging).

The registry is publicly browsable and searchable at https://cloudsecurityalliance.org/star/registry. Each entry corresponds to a cloud provider organization and lists their submitted assessments; Level 1 CAIQ submissions are downloadable as Excel/PDF files.

No per-entry SecID pattern is currently defined — bare `star` resolves to the registry homepage. Future work could add a child pattern for organization slugs.
